summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would require affordable rental housing conditions when Commonwealth land is sold or leased long term for residential development, subject to specified exemptions.
By default, at least 30% of dwellings would be affordable, with rent limited to the lower of 75% of market rent and 30% of household income.
Exemptions would cover small or significantly contaminated sites, prescribed remote or low-demand markets, specified Northern Territory land and land unsuitable for residential development.
changes: Covered disposals would include leases lasting at least 50 years, counting renewal options.
A recognised instrument under local land law would have to be ready before a disposal could be completed.
Registered not-for-profit community housing providers would manage the affordable dwellings.
Material breaches of affordable housing conditions could attract a civil penalty of up to 10,000 penalty units.
Tenant income eligibility would be assessed at the start of a tenancy without ongoing reassessment.
summary.affected: Commonwealth landholding entities, developers, community housing providers and eligible renter households are affected.
